name: Friars Hill
questions: Daft's header says 2 bathrooms but the description lists only a family bathroom. Is there an en suite, shower room or WC, and can you send a floor plan with room sizes, including the kitchen?
How big is the site, and where are the boundaries? Is the long building just north-east of the house the 'large garage', and is any of the fenced field behind the house included?
Has the house been lived in recently? If it has been vacant for two years or more, is it a probate sale, and can you confirm the vacancy dates (for the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant)?
How old are the oil boiler, windows, wiring and septic tank? Is there a septic tank certificate or a BER advisory report?
Is there a footpath from the gate into Thomastown along the Waterford Road, and has the site, the drive or the road ever flooded?

ai.why: Single-storey 4-bed with every bedroom on the ground floor, a walk from Thomastown's GP, schools and Dublin train, at €290k. Against it: one confirmed bathroom for six, a full renovation (roughly €90–155k), and about half an acre in a ribbon of houses on the R448 rather than the acre the brief wants.

electricity.detail: Connected; a furnished, recently occupied house, though the listing doesn't state the supply.

water.detail: Mains water, stated in the description.

sewer.detail: Septic tank, stated in the description. Ask its age and for a certificate.

internet.detail: Full fibre at the address per BuyerIQ ('Fast broadband: 387 Mb full fibre'); the listing doesn't mention broadband. Thomastown is on open eir FTTH; provider not confirmed.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: Single-storey bungalow (the aerial lead photo shows no upper floor or roof windows), so all four bedrooms are on the ground floor; there is no floor plan to name the best room for Gabor's parents.

bedsNote: Four 'generous' bedrooms plus two reception rooms (sitting room with open fire, living room with stove). Only one family bathroom is described; Daft's header says 2 baths, unconfirmed. Large detached garage.
heating: Oil-fired central heating; open fire in the sitting room, wood-burning stove in the living room
tagline: A dated single-storey 4-bed of 130 m² on an elevated half-acre above the Nore, on the Waterford Road about 1 km south of Thomastown.

pros.detail: €2,231/m² and stamp duty about €2,900, which leaves room for a full renovation and still lands around €380–450k all-in.

pros.text: Every bedroom on the ground floor
pros.detail: Single-storey bungalow, 130 m², four bedrooms on one level and no stairs.
About 1 km (14 min on foot by OSM routing) to Market Street: GP, pharmacy, Daybreak shop, cafés and Tābú; SuperValu and Lidl about 2 km.
Thomastown station is about 2.2 km on foot (the listing's '10 minutes' is optimistic) or a few minutes' drive; about 7 trains each weekday on the Waterford–Heuston line, roughly 1h45–2h.

pros.text: Schools in town, bus from the gate
pros.detail: St Mary's NS (about 430 pupils, new building 2010) and Grennan College (1.6 km) are in Thomastown, and the listing says a school bus picks up at the property.
The house sits about 30 m back from the road behind a lawn and tarmac drive, with fields across the road and the wooded river valley about 200 m below to the north-west.
Sitting room with an open fire in a stone surround and timber panelling, living room with a stove, solid wood floors; large detached garage.
St Luke's, Kilkenny (all ages) is about 19 km by road; University Hospital Waterford is the alternative.

cons.detail: Rough: second bathroom €12–20k (more if it needs an extension), D2 to B-rated insulation, windows and heat pump €45–70k before about €15–25k of SEAI grants, kitchen €15–25k, rewiring, plumbing and finishes €20–40k. The listing doesn't say it's vacant and the photos show furnished rooms; if it has been empty two years or more, the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant (up to €50k) could apply.
The description lists only a family bathroom; Daft's header says 2 baths, and there's no floor plan to settle it.

cons.text: About half an acre, not one
cons.detail: Satellite estimate 0.4–0.55 ac (0.16–0.22 ha). The enclosed rear garden looks shallow, ending at a hedge and post-and-rail fence 10–15 m behind the house; the front lawn runs to the R448 and would need fencing for the dogs.

cons.text: Houses either side, on the R448
cons.detail: It's one of about ten houses strung along the Waterford Road (R448, the old N9) at the gate. A long building about 12 m north-east may be the garage or a neighbour's house; other houses are about 25–45 m away, and a cluttered materials yard sits about 230 m south across the road.

cons.text: BER D2, oil and solid fuel
cons.detail: 286 kWh/m²/yr on oil central heating, with an open fire and a stove; running costs will be high until it's upgraded.
130 m² must hold four 'generous' bedrooms and two reception rooms, so the fitted kitchen may be small; no floor plan or dimensions are published.
Grennan College is small and DEIS; Scoil Aireagail in Ballyhale (about 12 km) has good progression, and St Kieran's and Kilkenny College are about 18 km away in the city.

BuyerIQ shows one hidden critical finding and seven high-priority flags (paid report), and 10 planning applications within 1 km, one an active build; septic tank age and any river flooding on the road aren't stated.
